title: Digital Safety Lab: Fraud Protection
learningGoals: Differentiate between legitimate and fraudulent payment requests
Understand that PIN is only for SENDING money, not RECEIVING
Identify red flags in suspicious messages

teachingScript.teacherLine: Listen carefully! This is the most important lesson in digital safety: You enter your UPI PIN ONLY to SEND money. You NEVER need a PIN to RECEIVE money.

sections.label: NEVER use PIN
items: If a stranger sends a request

teachingScript.teacherLine: What about OTP (One Time Password)? This is the final lock on your money. Never share your OTP with anyone — not even the bank!

data.title: The OTP Guard
points: Sharing it = Giving access to your bank
data.takeaway: If someone asks for an OTP over a call, it's a SCAM!

teachingScript.teacherLine: Time for a live test! You will receive 4 messages on this phone. Based on what you've learned, decide: should you Trust, Block, or Report?

questionPool.questionText: A stranger sends you a payment request for ₹500 and says 'Enter PIN to collect your prize!'. What do you do?
questionPool.hint: Remember the PIN rule: Only for SENDING.
